units.leftText: Now in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
units.rightText: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was among the exiles by the River Kebar, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.
leftNotes: 1:1 The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים*” (Elohim).
rightNotes: 1:1 Or from God

units.leftText: In the fifth of the month, which was the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s captivity,
units.rightText: On the fifth day of the month— it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin—

units.leftText: the LORD’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the LORD’s hand was there on him.
units.rightText: the word of the LORD came directly to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Kebar. And there the LORD’s hand was upon him.
leftNotes: 1:3 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).
rightNotes: 1:3 That is, the Babylonians

units.leftText: I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came out of the north: a great cloud, with flashing lightning, and a brightness around it, and out of the middle of it as it were glowing metal, out of the middle of the fire.
units.rightText: I looked and saw a whirlwind coming from the north, a great cloud with fire flashing back and forth and brilliant light all around it. In the center of the fire was a gleam like amber,
leftNotes: 1:4 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.
rightNotes: 1:4 Or The center of the fire looked like glowing metal; similarly in verse 27

units.leftText: Out of its center came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: They had the likeness of a man.
units.rightText: and within it was the form of four living creatures.

units.leftText: Everyone had four faces, and each one of them had four wings.
units.rightText: but each had four faces and four wings.

units.leftText: Their feet were straight feet. The sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot; and they sparkled like burnished bronze.
units.rightText: Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the hooves of a calf, gleaming like polished bronze.

units.leftText: They had the hands of a man under their wings on their four sides. The four of them had their faces and their wings like this:
units.rightText: Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. All four living creatures had faces and wings,

units.leftText: Their wings were joined to one another. They didn’t turn when they went. Each one went straight forward.
units.rightText: and their wings were touching one another. They did not turn as they moved; each one went straight ahead.

units.leftText: As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man. The four of them had the face of a lion on the right side. The four of them had the face of an ox on the left side. The four of them also had the face of an eagle.
units.rightText: The form of their faces was that of a man, and each of the four had the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle.

units.leftText: Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above. Two wings of each one touched another, and two covered their bodies.
units.rightText: Such were their faces.

units.leftText: Each one went straight forward. Where the spirit was to go, they went. They didn’t turn when they went.
units.rightText: Each creature went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, without turning as they moved.

units.leftText: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. The fire went up and down among the living creatures. The fire was bright, and lightning went out of the fire.
units.rightText: In the midst of the living creatures was the appearance of glowing coals of fire, or of torches. Fire moved back and forth between the living creatures; it was bright, and lightning flashed out of it.

units.leftText: The living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.
units.rightText: The creatures were darting back and forth as quickly as flashes of lightning.

units.leftText: Now as I saw the living creatures, behold, there was one wheel on the earth beside the living creatures, for each of the four faces of it.
units.rightText: When I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each creature with its four faces.

units.leftText: The appearance of the wheels and their work was like a beryl. The four of them had one likeness. Their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel within a wheel.
units.rightText: The workmanship of the wheels looked like the gleam of beryl, and all four had the same likeness. Their workmanship looked like a wheel within a wheel.

units.leftText: When they went, they went in their four directions. They didn’t turn when they went.
units.rightText: As they moved, they went in any of the four directions, without pivoting as they moved.

units.leftText: As for their rims, they were high and dreadful; and the four of them had their rims full of eyes all around.
units.rightText: Their rims were high and awesome, and all four rims were full of eyes all around.

units.leftText: When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them. When the living creatures were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up.
units.rightText: So as the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them, and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels also rose.

units.leftText: Wherever the spirit was to go, they went. The spirit was to go there. The wheels were lifted up beside them; for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
units.rightText: Wherever the spirit would go, they would go, and the wheels would rise alongside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

units.leftText: When those went, these went. When those stood, these stood. When those were lifted up from the earth, the wheels were lifted up beside them; for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
units.rightText: When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when the creatures stood still, the wheels stood still; and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose alongside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

units.leftText: Over the head of the living creature there was the likeness of an expanse, like an awesome crystal to look at, stretched out over their heads above.
units.rightText: Spread out above the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of an awesome expanse, gleaming like crystal.

units.leftText: Under the expanse, their wings were straight, one toward the other. Each one had two which covered on this side, and each one had two which covered their bodies on that side.
units.rightText: And under the expanse, their wings stretched out toward one another. Each one also had two wings covering its body.

units.leftText: When they went, I heard the noise of their wings like the noise of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a noise of tumult like the noise of an army. When they stood, they let down their wings.
units.rightText: When the creatures moved, I heard the sound of their wings like the roar of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army.
rightNotes: 1:24 Hebrew Shaddai

units.leftText: There was a voice above the expanse that was over their heads. When they stood, they let down their wings.
units.rightText: And there came a voice from above the expanse over their heads as they stood still with their wings lowered.

units.leftText: Above the expanse that was over their heads was the likeness of a throne, as the appearance of a sapphire stone. On the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man on it above.
units.rightText: Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne with the appearance of sapphire, and on the throne high above was a figure like that of a man.
leftNotes: 1:26 or, lapis lazuli

units.leftText: I saw as it were glowing metal, as the appearance of fire within it all around, from the appearance of his waist and upward; and from the appearance of his waist and downward I saw as it were the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him.
units.rightText: From what seemed to be His waist up, I saw a gleam like amber, with what looked like fire within it all around. And from what seemed to be His waist down, I saw what looked like fire; and brilliant light surrounded Him.

units.leftText: As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around.
units.rightText: The appearance of the brilliant light all around Him was like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell facedown and heard a voice speaking.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you.”
units.rightText: “Son of man, ” He said to me, “stand up on your feet and I will speak to you.”
rightNotes: 2:1 Or Son of Adam; here and throughout Ezekiel

units.leftText: The Spirit entered into me when he spoke to me, and set me on my feet; and I heard him who spoke to me.
units.rightText: And as He spoke to me, the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and I heard Him speaking to me.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, I send you to the children of Israel, to a nation of rebels who have rebelled against me. They and their fathers have transgressed against me even to this very day.
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “I am sending you to the Israelites, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me. To this very day they and their fathers have rebelled against Me.

units.leftText: The children are impudent and stiff-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’
units.rightText: They are obstinate and stubborn children. I am sending you to them, and you are to say to them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’
leftNotes: 2:4 The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.”

units.leftText: They, whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse—for they are a rebellious house—yet they will know that there has been a prophet among them.
units.rightText: And whether they listen or refuse to listen— for they are a rebellious house— they will know that a prophet has been among them.

units.leftText: You, son of man, don’t be afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you, and you dwell among scorpions. Don’t be afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.
units.rightText: But you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Do not be afraid, though briers and thorns surround you, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their presence, though they are a rebellious house.

units.leftText: You shall speak my words to them, whether they will hear or whether they will refuse; for they are most rebellious.
units.rightText: But speak My words to them, whether they listen or refuse to listen, for they are rebellious.

units.leftText: But you, son of man, hear what I tell you. Don’t be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth, and eat that which I give you.”
units.rightText: And you, son of man, listen to what I tell you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”

units.leftText: When I looked, behold, a hand was stretched out to me; and behold, a scroll of a book was in it.
units.rightText: Then I looked and saw a hand reaching out to me, and in it was a scroll,

units.leftText: He spread it before me. It was written within and without; and lamentations, mourning, and woe were written in it.
units.rightText: which He unrolled before me. And written on the front and back of it were words of lamentation, mourning, and woe.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel.”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.”

units.leftText: So I opened my mouth, and he caused me to eat the scroll.
units.rightText: So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll that I give you and fill your belly and your bowels with it.”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “eat and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.”

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel, and speak my words to them.
units.rightText: Then He said to me, “Son of man, go now to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.

units.leftText: For you are not sent to a people of a strange speech and of a hard language, but to the house of Israel—
units.rightText: For you are not being sent to a people of unfamiliar speech or difficult language, but to the house of Israel —

units.leftText: not to many peoples of a strange speech and of a hard language, whose words you can’t understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
units.rightText: not to the many peoples of unfamiliar speech and difficult language whose words you cannot understand. Surely if I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.

units.leftText: But the house of Israel will not listen to you, for they will not listen to me; for all the house of Israel are obstinate and hard-hearted.
units.rightText: But the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to you, since they are unwilling to listen to Me. For the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted.
leftNotes: 3:7 Literally, have a hard forehead

units.leftText: Behold, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their foreheads.
units.rightText: Behold, I will make your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads.

units.leftText: I have made your forehead as a diamond, harder than flint. Don’t be afraid of them, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.”
units.rightText: I will make your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed at their presence, even though they are a rebellious house.”

units.leftText: Moreover he said to me, “Son of man, receive in your heart and hear with your ears all my words that I speak to you.
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He added, “listen carefully to all the words I speak to you, and take them to heart.

units.leftText: Go to them of the captivity, to the children of your people, and speak to them, and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ whether they will hear, or whether they will refuse.”
units.rightText: Go to your people, the exiles; speak to them and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ whether they listen or refuse to listen.”

units.leftText: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing, saying, “Blessed be the LORD’s glory from his place.”
units.rightText: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard a great rumbling sound behind me: “Blessed be the glory of the LORD in His dwelling place!”
rightNotes: 3:12 Or the wind; also in verse 14
3:12 Or sound behind me as the glory of the LORD rose from its place!

units.leftText: I heard the noise of the wings of the living creatures as they touched one another, and the noise of the wheels beside them, even the noise of a great rushing.
units.rightText: It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another and the sound of the wheels beside them, a great rumbling sound.

units.leftText: So the Spirit lifted me up, and took me away; and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit; and the LORD’s hand was strong on me.
units.rightText: So the Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD upon me.

units.leftText: Then I came to them of the captivity at Tel Aviv who lived by the river Chebar, and to where they lived; and I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days.
units.rightText: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib who dwelt by the River Kebar. And for seven days I sat where they sat and remained there among them, overwhelmed.

units.leftText: At the end of seven days, the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: At the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel. Therefore hear the word from my mouth, and warn them from me.
units.rightText: “Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, give them a warning from Me.

units.leftText: When I tell the wicked, ‘You will surely die;’ and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity; but I will require his blood at your hand.
units.rightText: If I say to the wicked man, ‘You will surely die,’ but you do not warn him or speak out to warn him from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man will die in his iniquity, and I will hold you responsible for his blood.
rightNotes: 3:18 Or for his iniquity; also in verse 19

units.leftText: Yet if you warn the wicked, and he doesn’t turn from his wickedness, nor from his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.”
units.rightText: But if you warn a wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself.

units.leftText: “Again, when a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you have not given him warning, he will die in his sin, and his righteous deeds which he has done will not be remembered; but I will require his blood at your hand.
units.rightText: Now if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous acts he did will not be remembered. And I will hold you responsible for his blood.
rightNotes: 3:20 Or for his sin

units.leftText: Nevertheless if you warn the righteous man, that the righteous not sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live, because he took warning; and you have delivered your soul.”
units.rightText: But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will indeed live because he heeded your warning, and you will have saved yourself.”

units.leftText: The LORD’s hand was there on me; and he said to me, “Arise, go out into the plain, and I will talk with you there.”
units.rightText: And there the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He said to me, “Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you.”

units.leftText: Then I arose, and went out into the plain, and behold, the LORD’s glory stood there, like the glory which I saw by the river Chebar. Then I fell on my face.
units.rightText: So I got up and went out to the plain, and behold, the glory of the LORD was present there, like the glory I had seen by the River Kebar, and I fell facedown.

units.leftText: Then the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me, and said to me, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.
units.rightText: Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, “Go, shut yourself inside your house.

units.leftText: But you, son of man, behold, they will put ropes on you, and will bind you with them, and you will not go out among them.
units.rightText: And you, son of man, they will tie with ropes, and you will be bound so that you cannot go out among the people.

units.leftText: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you will be mute and will not be able to correct them, for they are a rebellious house.
units.rightText: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, and you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, though they are a rebellious house.

units.leftText: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house.”
units.rightText: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.[’’]

units.leftText: “You also, son of man, take a tile, and lay it before yourself, and portray on it a city, even Jerusalem.
units.rightText: “Now you, son of man, take a brick, place it before you, and draw on it the city of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Lay siege against it, build forts against it, and cast up a mound against it. Also set camps against it and plant battering rams against it all around.
units.rightText: Then lay siege against it: Construct a siege wall, build a ramp to it, set up camps against it, and place battering rams around it on all sides.

units.leftText: Take for yourself an iron pan and set it for a wall of iron between you and the city. Then set your face toward it. It will be besieged, and you shall lay siege against it. This shall be a sign to the house of Israel.
units.rightText: Then take an iron plate and set it up as an iron wall between yourself and the city. Turn your face toward it so that it is under siege, and besiege it. This will be a sign to the house of Israel.

units.leftText: “Moreover lie on your left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel on it. According to the number of the days that you shall lie on it, you shall bear their iniquity.
units.rightText: Then lie down on your left side and place the iniquity of the house of Israel upon yourself. You are to bear their iniquity for the number of days you lie on your side.

units.leftText: For I have appointed the years of their iniquity to be to you a number of days, even three hundred ninety days. So you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
units.rightText: For I have assigned to you 390 days, according to the number of years of their iniquity. So you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

units.leftText: “Again, when you have accomplished these, you shall lie on your right side, and shall bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. I have appointed forty days, each day for a year, to you.
units.rightText: When you have completed these days, lie down again, but on your right side, and bear the iniquity of the house of Judah. I have assigned to you 40 days, a day for each year.

units.leftText: You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm uncovered; and you shall prophesy against it.
units.rightText: You must turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.

units.leftText: Behold, I put ropes on you, and you shall not turn yourself from one side to the other, until you have accomplished the days of your siege.
units.rightText: Now behold, I will tie you up with ropes so you cannot turn from side to side until you have finished the days of your siege.

units.leftText: “Take for yourself also wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and put them in one vessel. Make bread of it. According to the number of the days that you will lie on your side, even three hundred ninety days, you shall eat of it.
units.rightText: But take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt; put them in a single container and make them into bread for yourself. This is what you are to eat during the 390 days you lie on your side.

units.leftText: Your food which you shall eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day. From time to time you shall eat it.
units.rightText: You are to weigh out twenty shekels of food to eat each day, and you are to eat it at set times.
leftNotes: 4:10 A shekel is about 10 grams or about 0.35 ounces.
rightNotes: 4:10 20 shekels is approximately 8 ounces or 228 grams of food.

units.leftText: You shall drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin. From time to time you shall drink.
units.rightText: You are also to measure out a sixth of a hin of water to drink, and you are to drink it at set times.
leftNotes: 4:11 A hin is about 6.5 liters or 1.7 gallons.
rightNotes: 4:11 A sixth of a hin is approximately 0.65 quarts or 0.61 liters of water.

units.leftText: You shall eat it as barley cakes, and you shall bake it in their sight with dung that comes out of man.”
units.rightText: And you shall eat the food as you would a barley cake, after you bake it over dried human excrement in the sight of the people.”

units.leftText: The LORD said, “Even thus will the children of Israel eat their bread unclean, among the nations where I will drive them.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD said, “This is how the Israelites will eat their defiled bread among the nations to which I will banish them.”

units.leftText: Then I said, “Ah Lord GOD! Behold, my soul has not been polluted; for from my youth up even until now I have not eaten of that which dies of itself, or is torn of animals. No abominable meat has come into my mouth!”
units.rightText: “Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now I have not eaten anything found dead or mauled by wild beasts. No unclean meat has ever entered my mouth.”
rightNotes: 4:14 Hebrew “Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “Behold, my soul has never been made unclean.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Behold, I have given you cow’s dung for man’s dung, and you shall prepare your bread on it.”
units.rightText: “Look,” He replied, “I will let you use cow dung instead of human excrement, and you may bake your bread over that.”

units.leftText: Moreover he said to me, “Son of man, behold, I will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight, and with fearfulness. They will drink water by measure, and in dismay;
units.rightText: Then He told me, “Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of food in Jerusalem. They will anxiously eat bread rationed by weight, and in despair they will drink water by measure.
rightNotes: 4:16 Hebrew staff

units.leftText: that they may lack bread and water, be dismayed one with another, and pine away in their iniquity.
units.rightText: So they will lack food and water; they will be appalled at the sight of one another wasting away in their iniquity.[’’]

units.leftText: “You, son of man, take a sharp sword. You shall take it as a barber’s razor to yourself, and shall cause it to pass over your head and over your beard. Then take balances to weigh and divide the hair.
units.rightText: “As for you, son of man, take a sharp sword, use it as a barber’s razor, and shave your head and beard. Then take a set of scales and divide the hair.

units.leftText: A third part you shall burn in the fire in the middle of the city, when the days of the siege are fulfilled. You shall take a third part, and strike with the sword around it. A third part you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw out a sword after them.
units.rightText: When the days of the siege have ended, you are to burn up a third of the hair inside the city; you are also to take a third and slash it with the sword all around the city; and you are to scatter a third to the wind. For I will unleash a sword behind them.

units.leftText: You shall take a small number of these and bind them in the folds of your robe.
units.rightText: But you are to take a few strands of hair and secure them in the folds of your garment.

units.leftText: Of these again you shall take, and cast them into the middle of the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it a fire will come out into all the house of Israel.
units.rightText: Again, take a few of these, throw them into the fire, and burn them. From there a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel.

units.leftText: “The Lord GOD says: ‘This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the middle of the nations, and countries are around her.
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD says: ‘This is Jerusalem, which I have set in the center of the nations, with countries all around her.

units.leftText: She has rebelled against my ordinances in doing wickedness more than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries that are around her; for they have rejected my ordinances, and as for my statutes, they have not walked in them.’
units.rightText: But she has rebelled against My ordinances more wickedly than the nations, and against My statutes worse than the countries around her. For her people have rejected My ordinances and have not walked in My statutes.’

units.leftText: “Therefore the Lord GOD says: ‘Because you are more turbulent than the nations that are around you, and have not walked in my statutes, neither have kept my ordinances, neither have followed the ordinances of the nations that are around you;
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘You have been more insubordinate than the nations around you; you have not walked in My statutes or kept My ordinances, nor have you even conformed to the ordinances of the nations around you.’
rightNotes: 5:7 Some Hebrew manuscripts and Syriac My ordinances; you have even conformed

units.leftText: therefore the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I, even I, am against you; and I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations.
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Behold, I Myself am against you, Jerusalem, and I will execute judgments among you in the sight of the nations.

units.leftText: I will do in you that which I have not done, and which I will not do anything like it any more, because of all your abominations.
units.rightText: Because of all your abominations, I will do to you what I have never done before and will never do again.

units.leftText: Therefore the fathers will eat the sons within you, and the sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments on you; and I will scatter the whole remnant of you to all the winds.
units.rightText: As a result, fathers among you will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter all your remnant to every wind.’

units.leftText: Therefore as I live,’ says the Lord GOD, ‘surely, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things, and with all your abominations, therefore I will also diminish you. My eye won’t spare, and I will have no pity.
units.rightText: Therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled My sanctuary with all your detestable idols and abominations, I Myself will withdraw My favor; I will not look upon you with pity, nor will I spare you.

units.leftText: A third part of you will die with the pestilence, and they will be consumed with famine within you. A third part will fall by the sword around you. A third part I will scatter to all the winds, and will draw out a sword after them.
units.rightText: A third of your people will die by plague or be consumed by famine within you, a third will fall by the sword outside your walls, and a third I will scatter to every wind and unleash a sword behind them.

units.leftText: “‘Thus my anger will be accomplished, and I will cause my wrath toward them to rest, and I will be comforted. They will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my zeal, when I have accomplished my wrath on them.
units.rightText: And when My anger is spent and I have vented My wrath against them, I will be appeased. And when I have spent My wrath on them, they will know that I, the LORD, in My zeal have spoken.

units.leftText: “‘Moreover I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of all that pass by.
units.rightText: I will make you a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of all who pass by.

units.leftText: So it will be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment, to the nations that are around you, when I execute judgments on you in anger and in wrath, and in wrathful rebukes—I, the LORD, have spoken it—
units.rightText: So you will be a reproach and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I execute judgments against you in anger, wrath, and raging fury. I, the LORD, have spoken.
rightNotes: 5:15 DSS, LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate; MT So it will be

units.leftText: when I send on them the evil arrows of famine that are for destruction, which I will send to destroy you. I will increase the famine on you and will break your staff of bread.
units.rightText: When I shower you with the deadly arrows of famine and destruction that I will send to destroy you, I will intensify the famine against you and cut off your supply of food.
rightNotes: 5:16 Hebrew them
5:16 Hebrew staff

units.leftText: I will send on you famine and evil animals, and they will bereave you. Pestilence and blood will pass through you. I will bring the sword on you. I, the LORD, have spoken it.’”
units.rightText: I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will leave you childless. Plague and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will bring a sword against you. I, the LORD, have spoken.”

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy to them,
units.rightText: “Son of man, set your face against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

units.leftText: and say, ‘You mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! The Lord GOD says to the mountains and to the hills, to the watercourses and to the valleys: “Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword on you, and I will destroy your high places.
units.rightText: You are to say: ‘O mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: I am about to bring a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.

units.leftText: Your altars will become desolate, and your incense altars will be broken. I will cast down your slain men before your idols.
units.rightText: Your altars will be demolished and your incense altars will be smashed; and I will cast down your slain before your idols.

units.leftText: I will lay the dead bodies of the children of Israel before their idols. I will scatter your bones around your altars.
units.rightText: I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols and scatter your bones around your altars.

units.leftText: In all your dwelling places, the cities will be laid waste and the high places will be desolate, so that your altars may be laid waste and made desolate, and your idols may be broken and cease, and your incense altars may be cut down, and your works may be abolished.
units.rightText: Wherever you live, the cities will be laid waste and the high places will be demolished, so that your altars will be laid waste and desecrated, your idols smashed and obliterated, your incense altars cut down, and your works blotted out.

units.leftText: The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
units.rightText: The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD.

units.leftText: “‘“Yet I will leave a remnant, in that you will have some that escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the countries.
units.rightText: Yet I will leave a remnant, for some of you will escape the sword when you are scattered among the nations and throughout the lands.

units.leftText: Those of you that escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their lewd heart, which has departed from me, and with their eyes, which play the prostitute after their idols. Then they will loathe themselves in their own sight for the evils which they have committed in all their abominations.
units.rightText: Then in the nations to which they have been carried captive, your survivors will remember Me — how I have been grieved by their adulterous hearts that turned away from Me, and by their eyes that lusted after idols. So they will loathe themselves for the evil they have done and for all their abominations.

units.leftText: They will know that I am the LORD. I have not said in vain that I would do this evil to them.”’
units.rightText: And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not declare in vain that I would bring this calamity upon them.

units.leftText: “The Lord GOD says: ‘Strike with your hand, and stamp with your foot, and say, “Alas!”, because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel; for they will fall by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence.
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stomp your feet, and cry out “Alas!” because of all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel, who will fall by sword and famine and plague.

units.leftText: He who is far off will die of the pestilence. He who is near will fall by the sword. He who remains and is besieged will die by the famine. Thus I will accomplish my wrath on them.
units.rightText: He who is far off will die by the plague, he who is near will fall by the sword, and he who remains will die by famine. So I will vent My fury upon them.

units.leftText: You will know that I am the LORD when their slain men are among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, under every green tree, and under every thick oak—the places where they offered pleasant aroma to all their idols.
units.rightText: Then you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, and under every green tree and leafy oak— the places where they offered fragrant incense to all their idols.

units.leftText: I will stretch out my hand on them and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness toward Diblah, throughout all their habitations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
units.rightText: I will stretch out My hand against them, and wherever they live I will make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
rightNotes: 6:14 Most Hebrew manuscripts; Vulgate and a few Hebrew manuscripts Riblah

units.leftText: Moreover the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “You, son of man, the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel, ‘An end! The end has come on the four corners of the land.
units.rightText: “O son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel:

units.leftText: Now the end is on you, and I will send my anger on you, and will judge you according to your ways. I will bring on you all your abominations.
units.rightText: The end is now upon you,

units.leftText: My eye will not spare you, neither will I have pity; but I will bring your ways on you, and your abominations will be among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’
units.rightText: I will not look on you with pity,

units.leftText: “The Lord GOD says: ‘A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD says:

units.leftText: An end has come. The end has come! It awakes against you. Behold, it comes.
units.rightText: The end has come!

units.leftText: Your doom has come to you, inhabitant of the land! The time has come! The day is near, a day of tumult, and not of joyful shouting, on the mountains.
units.rightText: Doom has come to you,

units.leftText: Now I will shortly pour out my wrath on you, and accomplish my anger against you, and will judge you according to your ways. I will bring on you all your abominations.
units.rightText: Very soon I will pour out My wrath upon you

units.leftText: My eye won’t spare, neither will I have pity. I will punish you according to your ways. Your abominations will be among you. Then you will know that I, the LORD, strike.
units.rightText: I will not look on you with pity,

units.leftText: “‘Behold, the day! Behold, it comes! Your doom has gone out. The rod has blossomed. Pride has budded.
units.rightText: Behold, the day is here!

units.leftText: Violence has risen up into a rod of wickedness. None of them will remain, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth. There will be nothing of value among them.
units.rightText: Their violence has grown into a rod

units.leftText: The time has come! The day draws near. Don’t let the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn; for wrath is on all its multitude.
units.rightText: The time has come;

units.leftText: For the seller won’t return to that which is sold, although they are still alive; for the vision concerns the whole multitude of it. None will return. None will strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.
units.rightText: The seller will surely not recover what he sold

units.leftText: They have blown the trumpet, and have made all ready; but no one goes to the battle, for my wrath is on all its multitude.
units.rightText: They have blown the trumpet

units.leftText: “‘The sword is outside, and the pestilence and the famine within. He who is in the field will die by the sword. He who is in the city will be devoured by famine and pestilence.
units.rightText: The sword is outside;

units.leftText: But of those who escape, they will escape and will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, everyone in his iniquity.
units.rightText: The survivors will escape

units.leftText: All hands will be feeble, and all knees will be weak as water.
units.rightText: Every hand will go limp,

units.leftText: They will also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and horror will cover them. Shame will be on all faces, and baldness on all their heads.
units.rightText: They will put on sackcloth,

units.leftText: They will cast their silver in the streets, and their gold will be as an unclean thing. Their silver and their gold won’t be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD’s wrath. They won’t satisfy their souls or fill their bellies; because it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.
units.rightText: They will throw their silver into the streets,

units.leftText: As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty; but they made the images of their abominations and their detestable things therein. Therefore I have made it to them as an unclean thing.
units.rightText: His beautiful ornaments

units.leftText: I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a plunder; and they will profane it.
units.rightText: And I will hand these things over

units.leftText: I will also turn my face from them, and they will profane my secret place. Robbers will enter into it, and profane it.
units.rightText: I will turn My face away from them,

units.leftText: “‘Make chains, for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.
units.rightText: Forge the chain,

units.leftText: Therefore I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will possess their houses. I will also make the pride of the strong to cease. Their holy places will be profaned.
units.rightText: So I will bring the most wicked of nations

units.leftText: Destruction comes! They will seek peace, and there will be none.
units.rightText: Anguish is coming!

units.leftText: Mischief will come on mischief, and rumor will be on rumor. They will seek a vision of the prophet; but the law will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.
units.rightText: Disaster upon disaster will come,

units.leftText: The king will mourn, and the prince will be clothed with desolation. The hands of the people of the land will be troubled. I will do to them after their way, and according to their own judgments I will judge them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
units.rightText: The king will mourn,

units.leftText: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in my house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, the Lord GOD’s hand fell on me there.
units.rightText: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me; and there the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me.

units.leftText: Then I saw, and behold, a likeness as the appearance of fire—from the appearance of his waist and downward, fire, and from his waist and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as it were glowing metal.
units.rightText: Then I looked and saw a figure like that of a man. From His waist down His appearance was like fire, and from His waist up He was as bright as the gleam of amber.
rightNotes: 8:2 Or as glowing metal

units.leftText: He stretched out the form of a hand, and took me by a lock of my head; and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and the sky, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the gate of the inner court that looks toward the north, where there was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy.
units.rightText: He stretched out what looked like a hand and took me by the hair of my head. Then the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and carried me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court, where the idol that provokes jealousy was seated.

units.leftText: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the appearance that I saw in the plain.
units.rightText: And there I saw the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the plain.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Son of man, lift up your eyes now the way toward the north.”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “now lift up your eyes to the north.”

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they do? Even the great abominations that the house of Israel commit here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? But you will again see yet other great abominations.”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what they are doing — the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing — to drive Me far from My sanctuary? Yet you will see even greater abominations.”

units.leftText: He brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold, a hole in the wall.
units.rightText: Then He brought me to the entrance to the court, and I looked and saw a hole in the wall.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Son of man, dig now in the wall.”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He told me, “dig through the wall.”

units.leftText: He said to me, “Go in, and see the wicked abominations that they do here.”
units.rightText: Then He said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are committing here.”

units.leftText: So I went in and looked, and saw every form of creeping things, abominable animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel, portrayed around on the wall.
units.rightText: So I went in and looked, and engraved all around the wall was every kind of crawling creature and detestable beast, along with all the idols of the house of Israel.

units.leftText: Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel stood before them. In the middle of them Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan stood, every man with his censer in his hand; and the smell of the cloud of incense went up.
units.rightText: Before them stood seventy elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had a censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense was rising.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, every man in his rooms of imagery? For they say, ‘The LORD doesn’t see us. The LORD has forsaken the land.’”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the darkness, each at the shrine of his own idol? For they are saying, ‘The LORD does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.’”

units.leftText: He said also to me, “You will again see more of the great abominations which they do.”
units.rightText: Again, He told me, “You will see them committing even greater abominations.”

units.leftText: Then he brought me to the door of the gate of the LORD’s house which was toward the north; and I saw the women sit there weeping for Tammuz.
units.rightText: Then He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and I saw women sitting there, weeping for Tammuz.
rightNotes: 8:14 Tammuz, meaning Sprout of Life, was a Sumerian god of fertility.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? You will again see yet greater abominations than these.”
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Yet you will see even greater abominations than these.”

units.leftText: He brought me into the inner court of the LORD’s house; and I saw at the door of the LORD’s temple, between the porch and the altar, there were about twenty-five men with their backs toward the LORD’s temple and their faces toward the east. They were worshiping the sun toward the east.
units.rightText: So He brought me to the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there at the entrance to the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east; and they were bowing to the east in worship of the sun.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations which they commit here? For they have filled the land with violence, and have turned again to provoke me to anger. Behold, they put the branch to their nose.
units.rightText: “Son of man,” He said to me, “do you see this? Is it not enough for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are practicing here, that they must also fill the land with violence and continually provoke Me to anger? Look, they are even putting the branch to their nose!

units.leftText: Therefore I will also deal in wrath. My eye won’t spare, neither will I have pity. Though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, yet I will not hear them.”
units.rightText: Therefore I will respond with wrath. I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. Although they shout loudly in My ears, I will not listen to them.”

units.leftText: Then he cried in my ears with a loud voice, saying, “Cause those who are in charge of the city to draw near, each man with his destroying weapon in his hand.”
units.rightText: Then I heard Him call out in a loud voice, saying, “Draw near, O executioners of the city, each with a weapon of destruction in hand.”

units.leftText: Behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate, which lies toward the north, every man with his slaughter weapon in his hand. One man in the middle of them was clothed in linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side. They went in, and stood beside the bronze altar.
units.rightText: And I saw six men coming from the direction of the Upper Gate, which faces north, each with a weapon of slaughter in his hand. With them was another man clothed in linen who had a writing kit at his side. And they came in and stood beside the bronze altar.

units.leftText: The glory of the God of Israel went up from the cherub, whereupon it was, to the threshold of the house; and he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side.
units.rightText: Then the glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherubim, where it had been, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And He called to the man clothed in linen who had the writing kit at his side.

units.leftText: The LORD said to him, “Go through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry over all the abominations that are done within it.”
units.rightText: “Go throughout the city of Jerusalem,” said the LORD, “and put a mark on the foreheads of the men sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there.”

units.leftText: To the others he said in my hearing, “Go through the city after him, and strike. Don’t let your eye spare, neither have pity.
units.rightText: And as I listened, He said to the others, “Follow him through the city and start killing; do not show pity or spare anyone!

units.leftText: Kill utterly the old man, the young man, the virgin, little children and women; but don’t come near any man on whom is the mark. Begin at my sanctuary.”
units.rightText: Slaughter the old men, the young men and maidens, the women and children; but do not go near anyone who has the mark. Now begin at My sanctuary.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!”
units.rightText: Then He told them, “Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go forth!”

units.leftText: While they were killing, and I was left, I fell on my face, and cried, and said, “Ah Lord GOD! Will you destroy all the residue of Israel in your pouring out of your wrath on Jerusalem?”
units.rightText: While they were killing, I was left alone. And I fell facedown and cried out, “Oh, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?”

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great, and the land is full of blood, and the city full of perversion; for they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land, and the LORD doesn’t see.’
units.rightText: He replied, “The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of perversity. For they say, ‘The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see.’

units.leftText: As for me also, my eye won’t spare, neither will I have pity, but I will bring their way on their head.”
units.rightText: But as for Me, I will not look on them with pity, nor will I spare them. I will bring their deeds down upon their own heads.”

units.leftText: Behold, the man clothed in linen, who had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, “I have done as you have commanded me.”
units.rightText: Then the man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his side reported back, “I have done as You commanded.”

units.leftText: Then I looked, and see, in the expanse that was over the head of the cherubim there appeared above them as it were a sapphire stone, as the appearance of the likeness of a throne.
units.rightText: And I looked and saw above the expanse, above the heads of the cherubim, the likeness of a throne of sapphire.
leftNotes: 10:1 or, lapis lazuli

units.leftText: He spoke to the man clothed in linen, and said, “Go in between the whirling wheels, even under the cherub, and fill both your hands with coals of fire from between the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.”
units.rightText: And the LORD said to the man clothed in linen, “Go inside the wheelwork beneath the cherubim. Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city.” And as I watched, he went in.

units.leftText: Now the cherubim stood on the right side of the house when the man went in; and the cloud filled the inner court.
units.rightText: Now when the man went in, the cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple, and a cloud filled the inner court.

units.leftText: The LORD’s glory mounted up from the cherub, and stood over the threshold of the house; and the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the LORD’s glory.
units.rightText: Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherubim and stood over the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the brightness of the glory of the LORD.

units.leftText: The sound of the wings of the cherubim was heard even to the outer court, as the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.
units.rightText: The sound of the wings of the cherubim could be heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when He speaks.
rightNotes: 10:5 Hebrew El-Shaddai

units.leftText: It came to pass, when he commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, “Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim,” that he went in and stood beside a wheel.
units.rightText: When the LORD commanded the man clothed in linen, saying, “Take fire from within the wheelwork, from among the cherubim,” the man went in and stood beside a wheel.

units.leftText: The cherub stretched out his hand from between the cherubim to the fire that was between the cherubim, and took some of it, and put it into the hands of him who was clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
units.rightText: Then one of the cherubim reached out his hand and took some of the fire that was among them. And he put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who received it and went out.

units.leftText: The form of a man’s hand appeared here in the cherubim under their wings.
units.rightText: (The cherubim appeared to have the form of human hands under their wings.)

units.leftText: I looked, and behold, there were four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub, and another wheel beside another cherub. The appearance of the wheels was like a beryl stone.
units.rightText: Then I looked and saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub. And the wheels gleamed like a beryl stone.

units.leftText: As for their appearance, the four of them had one likeness, like a wheel within a wheel.
units.rightText: As for their appearance, all four had the same form, like a wheel within a wheel.

units.leftText: When they went, they went in their four directions. They didn’t turn as they went, but to the place where the head looked they followed it. They didn’t turn as they went.
units.rightText: When they moved, they would go in any of the four directions, without turning as they moved. For wherever the head faced, the cherubim would go in that direction, without turning as they moved.

units.leftText: Their whole body, including their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around, even the wheels that the four of them had.
units.rightText: Their entire bodies, including their backs, hands, and wings, were full of eyes all around, as were their four wheels.

units.leftText: As for the wheels, they were called in my hearing, “the whirling wheels”.
units.rightText: I heard the wheels being called “the whirling wheels.”

units.leftText: Every one of them had four faces. The first face was the face of the cherub. The second face was the face of a man. The third face was the face of a lion. The fourth was the face of an eagle.
units.rightText: Each of the cherubim had four faces: the first face was that of a cherub, the second that of a man, the third that of a lion, and the fourth that of an eagle.

units.leftText: The cherubim mounted up. This is the living creature that I saw by the river Chebar.
units.rightText: Then the cherubim rose upward. These were the living creatures I had seen by the River Kebar.

units.leftText: When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them; and when the cherubim lifted up their wings to mount up from the earth, the wheels also didn’t turn from beside them.
units.rightText: When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them, and even when they spread their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not veer away from their side.

units.leftText: When they stood, these stood. When they mounted up, these mounted up with them; for the spirit of the living creature was in them.
units.rightText: When the cherubim stood still, the wheels also stood still, and when they ascended, the wheels ascended with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

units.leftText: The LORD’s glory went out from over the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.
units.rightText: Then the glory of the LORD moved away from the threshold of the temple and stood above the cherubim.

units.leftText: The cherubim lifted up their wings and mounted up from the earth in my sight when they went out, with the wheels beside them. Then they stood at the door of the east gate of the LORD’s house; and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
units.rightText: As I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose up from the ground, with the wheels beside them as they went. And they stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, with the glory of the God of Israel above them.

units.leftText: This is the living creature that I saw under the God of Israel by the river Chebar; and I knew that they were cherubim.
units.rightText: These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the River Kebar, and I knew that they were cherubim.

units.leftText: Every one had four faces, and every one four wings. The likeness of the hands of a man was under their wings.
units.rightText: Each had four faces and four wings, with what looked like human hands under their wings.

units.leftText: As for the likeness of their faces, they were the faces which I saw by the river Chebar, their appearances and themselves. They each went straight forward.
units.rightText: Their faces looked like the faces I had seen by the River Kebar. Each creature went straight ahead.

units.leftText: Moreover the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the LORD’s house, which looks eastward. Behold, twenty-five men were at the door of the gate; and I saw among them Jaazaniah the son of Azzur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people.
units.rightText: Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the gate of the house of the LORD that faces east. And there at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, who were leaders of the people.

units.leftText: He said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise iniquity, and who give wicked counsel in this city;
units.rightText: And the LORD said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who plot evil and give wicked counsel in this city.

units.leftText: who say, ‘The time is not near to build houses. This is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’
units.rightText: They are saying, ‘Is not the time near to build houses? The city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat.’
rightNotes: 11:3 Or cauldron

units.leftText: Therefore prophesy against them. Prophesy, son of man.”
units.rightText: Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, O son of man!”

units.leftText: The LORD’s Spirit fell on me, and he said to me, “Speak, ‘The LORD says: “Thus you have said, house of Israel; for I know the things that come into your mind.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me and told me to declare that this is what the LORD says: “That is what you are thinking, O house of Israel; and I know the thoughts that arise in your minds.

units.leftText: You have multiplied your slain in this city, and you have filled its streets with the slain.”
units.rightText: You have multiplied those you killed in this city and filled its streets with the dead.

units.leftText: “‘Therefore the Lord GOD says: “Your slain whom you have laid in the middle of it, they are the meat, and this is the cauldron; but you will be brought out of the middle of it.
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: The slain you have laid within this city are the meat, and the city is the pot; but I will remove you from it.

units.leftText: You have feared the sword; and I will bring the sword on you,” says the Lord GOD.
units.rightText: You fear the sword, so I will bring the sword against you, declares the Lord GOD.

units.leftText: “I will bring you out of the middle of it, and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and will execute judgments among you.
units.rightText: I will bring you out of the city and deliver you into the hands of foreigners, and I will execute judgments against you.

units.leftText: You will fall by the sword. I will judge you in the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
units.rightText: You will fall by the sword, and I will judge you even to the borders of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

units.leftText: This will not be your cauldron, neither will you be the meat in the middle of it. I will judge you in the border of Israel.
units.rightText: The city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be the meat within it. I will judge you even to the borders of Israel.

units.leftText: You will know that I am the LORD, for you have not walked in my statutes. You have not executed my ordinances, but have done after the ordinances of the nations that are around you.”’”
units.rightText: Then you will know that I am the LORD. For you have neither followed My statutes nor practiced My ordinances, but you have conformed to the ordinances of the nations around you.”

units.leftText: When I prophesied, Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died. Then I fell down on my face, and cried with a loud voice, and said, “Ah Lord GOD! Will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?”
units.rightText: Now as I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell facedown and cried out in a loud voice, “Oh, Lord GOD, will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end?”

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, your brothers, even your brothers, the men of your relatives, and all the house of Israel, all of them, are the ones to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, ‘Go far away from the LORD. This land has been given to us for a possession.’
units.rightText: “Son of man, your brothers — your relatives, your fellow exiles, and the whole house of Israel — are those of whom the people of Jerusalem have said, ‘They are far away from the LORD; this land has been given to us as a possession.’

units.leftText: “Therefore say, ‘The Lord GOD says: “Whereas I have removed them far off among the nations, and whereas I have scattered them among the countries, yet I will be to them a sanctuary for a little while in the countries where they have come.”’
units.rightText: Therefore declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘Although I sent them far away among the nations and scattered them among the countries, yet for a little while I have been a sanctuary for them in the countries to which they have gone.’

units.leftText: “Therefore say, ‘The Lord GOD says: “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.”
units.rightText: Therefore declare that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries to which you have been scattered, and I will give back to you the land of Israel.’

units.leftText: “‘They will come there, and they will take away all its detestable things and all its abominations from there.
units.rightText: When they return to it, they will remove all its detestable things and all its abominations.

units.leftText: I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them. I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them a heart of flesh,
units.rightText: And I will give them singleness of heart and put a new spirit within them; I will remove their heart of stone and give them a heart of flesh,

units.leftText: that they may walk in my statutes, and keep my ordinances, and do them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
units.rightText: so that they may follow My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them. Then they will be My people, and I will be their God.

units.leftText: But as for them whose heart walks after the heart of their detestable things and their abominations, I will bring their way on their own heads,’ says the Lord GOD.”
units.rightText: But as for those whose hearts pursue detestable things and abominations, I will bring their conduct down upon their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.”

units.leftText: Then the cherubim lifted up their wings, and the wheels were beside them. The glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
units.rightText: Then the cherubim, with the wheels beside them, spread their wings, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.

units.leftText: The LORD’s glory went up from the middle of the city, and stood on the mountain which is on the east side of the city.
units.rightText: And the glory of the LORD rose up from within the city and stood over the mountain east of the city.

units.leftText: The Spirit lifted me up, and brought me in the vision by the Spirit of God into Chaldea, to the captives.
units.rightText: And the Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to Chaldea, to the exiles in the vision given by the Spirit of God. After the vision had gone up from me,
rightNotes: 11:24 Or Babylonia

units.leftText: Then I spoke to the captives all the things that the LORD had shown me.
units.rightText: I told the exiles everything the LORD had shown me.

units.leftText: The LORD’s word also came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, you dwell in the middle of the rebellious house, who have eyes to see, and don’t see, who have ears to hear, and don’t hear; for they are a rebellious house.
units.rightText: “Son of man, you are living in a rebellious house. They have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear, for they are a rebellious house.

units.leftText: “Therefore, you son of man, prepare your baggage for moving, and move by day in their sight. You shall move from your place to another place in their sight. It may be they will consider, though they are a rebellious house.
units.rightText: Therefore, son of man, pack your bags for exile. In broad daylight, set out from your place and go to another as they watch. Perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house.

units.leftText: You shall bring out your baggage by day in their sight, as baggage for moving. You shall go out yourself at evening in their sight, as when men go out into exile.
units.rightText: Bring out your baggage for exile by day, as they watch. Then in the evening, as they watch, go out like those who go into exile.

units.leftText: Dig through the wall in their sight, and carry your baggage out that way.
units.rightText: As they watch, dig through the wall and carry your belongings out through it.

units.leftText: In their sight you shall bear it on your shoulder, and carry it out in the dark. You shall cover your face, so that you don’t see the land, for I have set you for a sign to the house of Israel.”
units.rightText: And as they watch, lift your bags to your shoulder and take them out at dusk; cover your face so that you cannot see the land. For I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.”

units.leftText: I did so as I was commanded. I brought out my baggage by day, as baggage for moving, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand. I brought it out in the dark, and bore it on my shoulder in their sight.
units.rightText: So I did as I was commanded. I brought out my bags for exile by day, and in the evening I dug through the wall by hand. I took my belongings out at dusk, carrying them on my shoulder as they watched.

units.leftText: In the morning, the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: And in the morning the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, hasn’t the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’
units.rightText: “Son of man, hasn’t the rebellious house of Israel asked you, ‘What are you doing?’

units.leftText: “Say to them, ‘The Lord GOD says: “This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem, and all the house of Israel among whom they are.”’
units.rightText: Tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘This burden concerns the prince in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are there.’

units.leftText: “Say, ‘I am your sign. As I have done, so will it be done to them. They will go into exile, into captivity.
units.rightText: You are to say, ‘I am a sign to you.’ Just as it happened here, so will it be done to them; they will go into exile as captives.
rightNotes: 12:11 Literally ‘I am a sign to you.’ Just as I have done; some translators close the quotation at the end of the verse.

units.leftText: “‘The prince who is among them will bear his baggage on his shoulder in the dark, and will go out. They will dig through the wall to carry things out that way. He will cover his face, because he will not see the land with his eyes.
units.rightText: And at dusk the prince among them will lift his bags to his shoulder and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out. He will cover his face so he cannot see the land.

units.leftText: I will also spread my net on him, and he will be taken in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldeans; yet he will not see it, though he will die there.
units.rightText: But I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans; yet he will not see it, and there he will die.

units.leftText: I will scatter toward every wind all who are around him to help him, and all his bands. I will draw out the sword after them.
units.rightText: And I will scatter to every wind all the attendants around him and all his troops, and I will draw a sword to chase after them.

units.leftText: “‘They will know that I am the LORD when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the countries.
units.rightText: And they will know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries.

units.leftText: But I will leave a few men of them from the sword, from the famine, and from the pestilence, that they may declare all their abominations among the nations where they come. Then they will know that I am the LORD.’”
units.rightText: But I will spare a few of them from sword and famine and plague, so that in the nations to which they go, they can recount all their abominations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”

units.leftText: Moreover the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Moreover, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, eat your bread with quaking, and drink your water with trembling and with fearfulness.
units.rightText: “Son of man, eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with quivering and anxiety.

units.leftText: Tell the people of the land, ‘The Lord GOD says concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem and the land of Israel: “They will eat their bread with fearfulness and drink their water in dismay, that her land may be desolate, and all that is therein, because of the violence of all those who dwell therein.
units.rightText: Then tell the people of the land that this is what the Lord GOD says about those living in Jerusalem and in the land of Israel: ‘They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dread, for their land will be stripped of everything in it because of the violence of all who dwell in it.

units.leftText: The cities that are inhabited will be laid waste, and the land will be a desolation. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”’”
units.rightText: The inhabited cities will be laid waste, and the land will become desolate. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel, saying, ‘The days are prolonged, and every vision fails’?
units.rightText: “Son of man, what is this proverb that you have in the land of Israel:

units.leftText: Tell them therefore, ‘The Lord GOD says: “I will make this proverb to cease, and they will no more use it as a proverb in Israel;”’ but tell them, ‘“The days are at hand, and the fulfillment of every vision.
units.rightText: Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘I will put an end to this proverb, and in Israel they will no longer recite it.’

units.leftText: For there will be no more any false vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel.
units.rightText: For there will be no more false visions or flattering divinations within the house of Israel,

units.leftText: For I am the LORD. I will speak, and the word that I speak will be performed. It will be no more deferred; for in your days, rebellious house, I will speak the word and will perform it,” says the Lord GOD.’”
units.rightText: because I, the LORD, will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be fulfilled without delay. For in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak a message and bring it to pass, declares the Lord GOD.’”

units.leftText: Again the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Furthermore, the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, behold, they of the house of Israel say, ‘The vision that he sees is for many days to come, and he prophesies of times that are far off.’
units.rightText: “Son of man, take note that the house of Israel is saying, ‘The vision that he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about the distant future.’

units.leftText: “Therefore tell them, ‘The Lord GOD says: “None of my words will be deferred any more, but the word which I speak will be performed,” says the Lord GOD.’”
units.rightText: Therefore tell them that this is what the Lord GOD says: ‘None of My words will be delayed any longer. The message I speak will be fulfilled, declares the Lord GOD.’”

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy, and say to those who prophesy out of their own heart, ‘Hear the LORD’s word:
units.rightText: “Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are now prophesying. Tell those who prophesy out of their own imagination: Hear the word of the LORD!

units.leftText: The Lord GOD says, “Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!
units.rightText: This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit yet have seen nothing.

units.leftText: Israel, your prophets have been like foxes in the waste places.
units.rightText: Your prophets, O Israel, are like foxes among the ruins.

units.leftText: You have not gone up into the gaps or built up the wall for the house of Israel, to stand in the battle in the LORD’s day.
